celery: celery: the package a project imports, and the message-bus technology its tasks run on
Celery: celery: the app class a project builds
current_app: celery: the object the library exports for whichever app is running
task: celery: the decorator on a Celery app that makes a function a task
shared_task: celery: the decorator the library exports that makes a function a task without an app
name: suss: the syntax field every adapter reads a definition's name from; also celery: the keyword a task decorator and send_task take the task's name under
queue: celery: the keyword a task decorator takes its queue under
delay: celery: the Task method that enqueues the task with the arguments it is given
apply_async: celery: the Task method that enqueues the task with its arguments packed as args and kwargs
send_task: celery: the Celery app method that enqueues a task by its name
args: celery: the keyword apply_async and send_task take the positional arguments under
kwargs: celery: the keyword apply_async and send_task take the keyword arguments under
modulePath: suss: the default task name Celery gives, the module path and the function's name
spread: suss: an enqueue that passes the task's arguments as its own
packed: suss: an enqueue that passes the task's arguments as one sequence and one mapping
